mainTopic: How 'עד' is read in measures, and טרפה rulings about the spleen and kidneys
overview: The amud opens by asking whether the word 'עד' (up to) includes the final number. The גמרא tests this with a משנה about broken clay vessels, which gives three size ranges: up to a לוג, from a לוג to a סאה, and from a סאה to two סאה. Each proof is pushed back, because each endpoint could belong to the upper range instead. Then a ברייתא says outright that each endpoint counts with the lower range. The גמרא answers with רבי יוחנן's rule that all שיעורי חכמים are read strictly, except the כגריס of כתמים. A ברייתא about a bed-rope supports this rule. Next the גמרא turns to the טחול: רב עוירא says a removed טחול is kosher but a pierced one makes the animal a טרפה. It defends him against a challenge from a משנה with two different answers. Finally it brings רב's ruling that disease in even one kidney makes the animal a טרפה, and a limit on that ruling from ארץ ישראל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof attempt from the first range: up to a לוג
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a broken clay vessel piece needs to hold enough oil to anoint a baby, for vessels 'up to a לוג.' The גמרא asks: doesn't this mean a vessel of exactly one לוג counts in this lower group?
steps.simpleTranslation: Their measure is enough to anoint a small child, and this applies up to a לוג. Doesn't this mean a vessel of exactly a לוג is treated like the smaller ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about broken clay vessels and tries to use it as proof that 'עד' includes the endpoint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a vessel of exactly one לוג falls under the lower rule (anointing a baby), then 'עד לוג' means 'up to and including a לוג.' That would support reading 'עד' as inclusive.

keyTerms.meaning: Their measure. Here, the minimum amount the broken piece must hold to still count as a vessel.
Anointing a small child. A tiny amount of oil.
A unit of liquid measure.
'Is it not that...?' A formula for suggesting a proof.
Like below. Treated as part of the smaller range.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the middle of a משנה quote that began just before. The bottoms and sides of broken clay vessels are being discussed, not whole vessels.

phrases.english: their measure is enough to anoint a small child
phrases.notes: This continues a משנה about the bottoms and sides of broken clay vessels: if they can hold this much, they still count as vessels for טומאה.

phrases.english: and this applies up to a log.
Is it not that a vessel of exactly a log is like below?
phrases.notes: 'Like below' means a vessel of exactly a לוג goes with the smaller group, so the endpoint is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof attempt begun before this section, quoting the משנה about broken clay vessels.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about broken clay vessel bottoms: 'ועד לוג.'

steps.title: Rejection: a לוג may belong to the upper range
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a vessel of exactly one לוג may be treated with the bigger vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A vessel of exactly a לוג is treated like the larger ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the endpoint could just as well belong to the higher group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a לוג-sized vessel goes with the upper range, then 'עד לוג' means 'up to but not including a לוג.' So the משנה proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Like above. Treated as part of the larger range.
Up to but not including. The reading this answer allows.

phrases.english: No, a log is like above.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully neutralizes the proof from the first range.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording allows the endpoint to belong to the upper range just as easily.

steps.title: Second proof attempt: from a לוג to a סאה
steps.stepSummary: The next part of the משנה says vessels from a לוג to a סאה need their broken piece to hold a רביעית. The גמרא asks whether a סאה-sized vessel goes with this lower group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: from a לוג to a סאה, the piece needs to hold a רביעית. Doesn't this mean a vessel of exactly a סאה is treated like the smaller ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again with the next line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same question now applies to the second range. If a vessel of exactly one סאה only needs a רביעית, then 'עד סאה' includes the סאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A larger measure, equal to 24 לוגין.
A quarter of a לוג.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִלּוֹג עַד סְאָה – בִּרְבִיעִית,
phrases.english: Come and hear: from a log up to a se'a, with a quarter-log,
Is it not that a se'a is like below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, tries the next clause of the same משנה.

steps.title: Rejection: a סאה may belong to the upper range
steps.stepSummary: Same answer as before: a סאה-sized vessel may go with the larger vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A vessel of exactly a סאה is treated like the larger ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof the same way it rejected the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ranges could be read as 'up to but not including.' In that case a סאה-sized vessel falls in the next range, which needs half a לוג. So again nothing is proven.

keyTerms.meaning: No. The Aramaic spelling, used to reject a proof.
The later part of a משנה. The proofs are moving down its clauses.
A rejection of a proof.

phrases.english: No, a se'a is like above.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Neutralizes the proof from the second range.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The endpoint can belong to the higher range.

steps.title: Third proof attempt: from a סאה to two סאה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: vessels from a סאה to two סאה need their broken piece to hold half a לוג. The גמרא asks whether two סאה goes with this lower group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: from a סאה up to two סאה, the piece needs to hold half a לוג. Doesn't this mean a vessel of exactly two סאה is treated like the smaller ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a third attempt using the next range in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same logic applies again. If a vessel of exactly two סאה only needs half a לוג, then 'עד' includes the endpoint.

keyTerms.meaning: Two סאה.
Half a לוג.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִסְּאָה וְעַד סָאתַיִם – בַּחֲצִי לוֹג,
phrases.english: Come and hear: from a se'a up to two se'a, with half a log,
Is it not that two se'a is like below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second proof was rejected, tries the third clause of the same משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'מסאה ועד סאתים בחצי לוג.'

steps.title: Rejection: two סאה may belong to the upper range
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא says the endpoint, two סאה, may belong with the larger vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A vessel of exactly two סאה is treated like the larger ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the third proof the same way as the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because every range in the משנה can be read either way, the משנה alone cannot decide whether 'עד' is inclusive. This sets up the need for a clearer source.

keyTerms.meaning: A required measure or amount.
The beginning and later parts of a source. None of the משנה's parts settles the question.
A proof. Here, a proof that has now failed three times.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about broken clay vessels can be read both ways. Each endpoint (לוג, סאה, סאתים) could belong to the lower or the upper range.

phrases.english: No, two se'a is like above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 5, ending the attempts based on the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Neutralizes the last proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The endpoint can belong to the higher range.

steps.title: A ברייתא says outright that every endpoint counts with the lower range
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states clearly that a לוג, a סאה, and two סאה each count with the smaller range. This means 'עד' includes the endpoint.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: a לוג is like below, a סאה is like below, two סאה is like below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that openly settles what the משנה left unclear. It uses this to challenge the view that 'עד' excludes the endpoint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejections in steps 2, 4, and 6 said each endpoint might belong to the upper range. This ברייתא says plainly that each one belongs to the lower range. So 'עד' here means 'up to and including,' which challenges the view (attributed to רב נחמן) that it does not include the endpoint.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה.
Up to and including. The reading the ברייתא supports.
'But is it not...?' Opens a challenge from a source.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says clearly that each endpoint (לוג, סאה, סאתים) counts with the lower range. That makes 'עד' inclusive here and challenges the opposite view.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether 'עד' includes the endpoint matters for many halachic measures. This ברייתא is a clear source on that question.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
a log is like below, a se'a is like below,
two se'a is like below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the three rejections by bringing an explicit source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejections in steps 2, 4 and 6, and the view that 'עד' excludes the endpoint.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא puts every endpoint in the lower range. That leaves no room for the 'כלמעלה' reading.

steps.title: There 'up to' included the endpoint because that was stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא about vessels read 'עד' as including the endpoint only because that was the strict reading. רבי יוחנן says all שיעורי חכמים are read strictly, except the כגריס of כתמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the endpoint was included to be strict. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: all measures of the חכמים are applied strictly, except for the bean-size measure of stains, which is applied leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 7. The endpoint was included there only because including it gave the stricter result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With vessels, counting the endpoint with the smaller range means a smaller broken piece still counts as a vessel, so it can become טמא. That is the strict side. רבי יוחנן's rule says measures always go the strict way, so in our case of טרפה we also take whichever reading is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: to be strict
the measures set by the Sages
the size of a bean (a split bean)
blood stains found on a woman's clothing
to be lenient

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'עד' always includes the endpoint or always leaves it out. The rule is that whichever reading is stricter wins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for reading measures: when a measure is unclear, go strict. The only exception is the stain measure.

phrases.english: There, it is in order to be strict.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא about vessels from the last step.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the measures of the Sages are to be applied strictly,
except for the bean-size of stains, which is applied leniently.
phrases.notes: A stain that is exactly bean-sized does not make the woman טמאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא's reading to cases where including the endpoint is the strict result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that 'עד' always includes the endpoint.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עד' is read whichever way is stricter. In the vessels case, that meant including the endpoint.

steps.title: Support from the bed-rope ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the strictness rule. A ברייתא on the bed-rope משנה treats five טפחים as above and ten as below, so both endpoints are read strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also shows this, for it teaches about that משנה: five is like above, ten is like below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that measures are read strictly. A ברייתא puts each endpoint wherever it makes the rope טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the bed-rope case, a rope under five טפחים is טהור, and a rope from five to ten is טמא. A rope of exactly five is put in the higher, טמא group. A rope of exactly ten is put in the lower, טמא group. The endpoint moves in different directions, but both times it lands on the strict side. This proves that strictness, not the word 'עד', decides.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording also shows this; a support
like the higher group
like the lower group

steps.whatToRemember: Unclear measures are read strictly, except for stains. That is why one endpoint can go up and the other go down.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
for it teaches about that one:
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה in כלים about a rope hanging from a bed: under five טפחים it is טהור, and from five to ten it is טמא.

phrases.english: five is like above,
ten is like below.
phrases.notes: Both choices put the rope in the טמא group, which is the strict result.

steps.raayaObject: The rule that measures are read strictly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the bed-rope משנה in כלים.

steps.title: Removed spleen is kosher, but a pierced one is not
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line 'ניטל הטחול', רב עוירא in the name of רבא limits the leniency: a removed טחול is kosher, but a pierced טחול makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If the spleen was removed.' רב עוירא said in the name of רבא: they taught this only when it was removed, but if it was pierced, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It brings a limit on that line's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an animal whose טחול was removed is still kosher. רב עוירא says that is true only when the whole טחול is gone. If it is pierced, the animal becomes a טרפה. This sounds surprising, which sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: spleen
was removed
was pierced (has a hole)
an animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten
they taught this only in the case of

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that removing the whole spleen is fine but a hole is not. That is the ruling as stated, and the next step challenges it.

phrases.english: 'If the spleen was removed.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which lists this among the cases that are kosher.

phrases.english: Rav Avira said in the name of Rava:
They taught this only when it was removed,
but if it was pierced, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a removed טחול keeps the animal kosher. A pierced טחול makes it a טרפה.

steps.title: Challenge from cutting pieces off the spleen
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין challenges רב עוירא from a משנה. It forbids pieces cut from the טחול but suggests the animal itself is permitted, so a damaged טחול does not make it a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין, and some say רבי יוסי בר זבידא, objected: if one cuts pieces from a fetus inside the animal, they may be eaten. If one cuts from the spleen or the kidneys, they may not be eaten. This implies that the animal itself is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge against רב עוירא's ruling that a pierced טחול makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids only the cut-off pieces of the טחול, because they were cut from a living animal. It does not forbid the animal itself. If cutting into the טחול does not make the animal a טרפה, then surely a hole in it should not either. That contradicts רב עוירא.

keyTerms.meaning: a fetus
kidneys
this implies; from this we learn

steps.confusionAlert: The pieces are forbidden only because they were cut off while the animal was alive. That is a different reason from טרפה, so it says nothing against the animal itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin raised an objection,
and some say it was Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida:
One who cuts from a fetus that is inside its mother,
it is permitted to eat,
but if from the spleen or from the kidneys,
it is forbidden to eat.
This implies the animal itself is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב עוירא's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עוירא's ruling that a pierced טחול makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids only the pieces cut from the טחול, which implies the animal stays kosher even though its טחול was damaged.

steps.title: The animal is forbidden too; the wording just matches the earlier clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the animal itself is also forbidden. The משנה wrote 'forbidden to eat' about the pieces only to match the wording of its earlier clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the same is true of the animal: it is forbidden too. But since the first part of the משנה said 'permitted to eat' about the parts of the fetus, the last part said 'forbidden to eat' about the pieces of the טחול, to make a matching contrast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is defending רב עוירא against the challenge from the משנה. It explains that the משנה's wording does not prove the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר אבין had argued that the משנה only forbids the pieces, so the animal must be permitted. The answer is that the משנה chose its words to mirror the earlier clause, not to exclude the animal. So the animal can still be a טרפה, just as רב עוירא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies; 'the same is true of'
Since, because of; used when a wording was chosen to match another wording
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is saying that only the pieces are forbidden. According to this answer, the whole animal is forbidden. The words 'forbidden to eat' were just chosen to match the earlier 'permitted to eat.'

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּהֵמָה נָמֵי אֲסִירָא,
phrases.english: The same is true: even the animal is also forbidden,
but since it taught in the first clause 'permitted to eat,'
phrases.notes: The first clause is about the parts of the fetus.

phrases.english: it also taught in the last clause 'forbidden to eat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּהֵמָה נָמֵי אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רבי יוסי בר אבין from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic wording explanation: the phrase 'forbidden to eat' was chosen to parallel the earlier clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids only the pieces of the טחול, so the animal itself is kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal is forbidden too. The משנה's wording only mirrors the 'permitted to eat' of the earlier clause.

steps.title: A pierced spleen and a cut spleen are different cases
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: a pierced טחול and a cut טחול are separate cases with different laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: a pierced טחול is one case, and a cut טחול is a different case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the challenge. The משנה is talking about a cut טחול, while רב עוירא is talking about a pierced one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, the משנה really does mean the animal stays permitted, but only when the טחול was cut. A hole (ניקב) is a different kind of damage, and there רב עוירא's ruling of טרפה still stands. So the משנה does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say; introduces an alternative answer
Pierced, has a hole
Cut; a piece was cut off
Separately; a case of its own

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to defend רב עוירא. (1) The animal is also forbidden, and the משנה's wording is just for matching. (2) A cut טחול leaves the animal permitted, but a pierced טחול makes it a טרפה.

phrases.english: Or, if you wish, say:
pierced is its own case, and cut is its own case.
phrases.notes: He means a pierced טחול makes the animal a טרפה, but a cut one does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: נִיקַּב לְחוֹד, וְנֶחְתַּךְ לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the same קשיא answered in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the משנה speaks of a cut טחול, while רב עוירא speaks of a pierced one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any damage to the טחול is treated the same, so the משנה's permitted animal contradicts רב עוירא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cut טחול leaves the animal permitted, but a pierced טחול makes it a טרפה.

steps.title: Disease in even one kidney makes the animal a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case 'the kidneys were removed,' רכיש בר פפא says in the name of רב that disease in even one kidney makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the kidneys were removed, the animal is kosher. רכיש בר פפא said in the name of רב: if an animal is diseased in even one kidney, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line in the משנה, about kidneys, and brings a new ruling from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the טחול discussion. Removing the organ completely does not make the animal a טרפה, but disease in it does. רב says even one diseased kidney is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Kidneys (singular: כּוּלְיָא)
Was stricken or diseased
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Removing a kidney does not make the animal a טרפה, but a diseased kidney does. Disease is treated more strictly than removal.

phrases.english: 'The kidneys were removed.'
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says the animal is still kosher in this case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rakhish bar Pappa said in the name of Rav:
If it was diseased in one kidney, it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיטְּלוּ הַכְּלָיוֹת. אָמַר רָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טחול discussion and starts a new topic on the next case in the משנה, the kidneys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal with disease in even one kidney is a טרפה, even though removing the kidneys does not make it one.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל limits the kidney ruling
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל start to limit רב's ruling: it applies only when the disease has reached a certain point. The sentence continues on the next part of the דף.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say: this ruling applies only when the disease has reached...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a limit to רב's ruling from the scholars of ארץ ישראל. The statement is cut off here, and the limit is finished in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'והוא ד' mean 'and that is only when.' They show that the טרפה ruling of step 14 does not cover every disease in a kidney. It applies only once the disease reaches a certain place, which the text names right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West'; the גמרא's name for ארץ ישראל
And that is only when; introduces a limit on a ruling
The disease or damage

phrases.english: They say in the West:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: And that is only where the disease reached

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 14 so it applies only to disease that reached a certain point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A diseased kidney makes the animal a טרפה only when the disease has reached a certain place. That place is named in the text that follows.
